title: PTGui Tutorial Part 5: HDR Panorama Stitching
summary: This PTGui tutorial segment explains HDR panorama workflows in the Pro edition, detailing the theory of high dynamic range, the practical capture workflow for bracketed images, and how PTGui stitches and tone-maps multiple exposures into a single panorama. It compares true HDR merging with exposure fusion, demonstrates linking bracketed exposures to preserve alignment, and covers output options (32‑bit panoramas, layer exports, and tone-mapping in PTGui versus Photoshop). The speaker emphasizes rigid capture practices (tripod, static scene, fixed aperture/ISO), and shows how to export and review HDR results, including 32-bit workflows in Photoshop.

sections.description: The video opens with an overview of HDR concepts as they pertain to panoramic photography, defining 32-bit linear HDR files and the need for tone mapping to render scenes with extreme brightness contrasts. It explains why multiple exposures are bracketed and how a single JPEG cannot preserve true brightness levels, setting the stage for PTGui's HDR workflow.

sections.description: This section covers the capture workflow, emphasizing consistent bracketing across viewing directions, TROUBLESTS with alignment, and the practical steps to ensure sharp panorama data. It introduces PTGui’s linking feature, which associates bracketed images so yaw/pitch/roll are preserved across the stack, improving control point generation and final stitching.

The presenter explains that PTGui merges the separate exposure planes first and then tones them, and demonstrates how to access and adjust HDR-specific controls to influence brightness, contrast, and saturation within the panorama.
